events.title: Dalton's Atomic Theory
events.detail: John Dalton proposed atoms as tiny indivisible solid spheres — the foundation of modern atomic theory.

events.title: Discovery of the Electron
events.detail: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron, proving atoms contain negatively charged particles.

events.title: Rutherford's Gold Foil Experiment
events.detail: Ernest Rutherford discovered the nucleus — atoms have a tiny dense positive core with electrons orbiting.

events.title: Bohr's Atomic Model
events.detail: Niels Bohr proposed electrons occupy fixed energy levels around the nucleus, explaining atomic spectra.

events.title: Discovery of the Neutron
events.detail: James Chadwick discovered neutrons, completing the picture of atomic structure (protons + neutrons + electrons).

events.title: Quantum Mechanical Model
events.detail: Erwin Schrödinger developed the wave equation, replacing orbits with probability clouds (orbitals).

events.title: Döbereiner's Triads
events.detail: Johann Döbereiner noticed patterns in groups of three similar elements, the first periodic observation.

events.title: Newlands' Law of Octaves
events.detail: John Newlands proposed elements repeat properties every 8th element, but the pattern broke after calcium.

events.title: Mendeleev's Periodic Table
events.detail: Dmitri Mendeleev arranged 63 elements by atomic weight and left gaps for undiscovered elements — a breakthrough.

events.title: Moseley's Refinement
events.detail: Henry Moseley reorganized the table by atomic number (not weight), explaining why some elements seemed out of order.

events.title: Synthetic Elements Added
events.detail: Post-WWII, scientists synthesized elements beyond uranium (Plutonium, Americium), expanding the periodic table.

events.title: Four New Elements Named
events.detail: Flerovium, Livermorium, Moscovium, and Oganesson officially named, completing the 7th period of the periodic table.

events.title: DNA First Isolated
events.detail: Friedrich Miescher isolated 'nuclein' from white blood cell nuclei — the first isolation of DNA.

events.title: DNA Building Blocks Identified
events.detail: Phoebus Levene identified the components: four bases (A, T, G, C), deoxyribose sugar, and phosphate groups.

events.title: DNA Carries Genetic Information
events.detail: Oswald Avery proved DNA (not protein) is the molecule that carries hereditary information in bacteria.

events.title: Chargaff's Rules
events.detail: Erwin Chargaff discovered DNA has equal amounts of A-T and G-C, hinting at base pairing.

events.title: X-ray Crystallography Begins
events.detail: Rosalind Franklin's Photo 51 revealed DNA's helical structure through brilliant X-ray diffraction work.

events.title: Double Helix Model
events.detail: Watson, Crick, and Franklin revealed DNA's famous double helix structure with complementary base pairing.

events.title: Corpuscular vs Wave Debate
events.detail: Isaac Newton proposed light as particles (corpuscles); Christiaan Huygens proposed light as waves.

events.title: Young's Double Slit Experiment
events.detail: Thomas Young proved light produces interference patterns — strong evidence light behaves as a wave.

events.title: Light as Electromagnetic Waves
events.detail: James Clerk Maxwell unified electricity & magnetism, proving light is an electromagnetic wave.

events.title: Planck's Quantum Hypothesis
events.detail: Max Planck proposed light comes in discrete packets (quanta/photons) to explain blackbody radiation.

events.title: Photoelectric Effect
events.detail: Einstein explained the photoelectric effect using Planck's photons — light acts as particles at the atomic scale.

events.title: Wave-Particle Duality Confirmed
events.detail: Davisson & Germer showed electrons exhibit diffraction (wave behavior), confirming particles have wave properties.

events.title: Battle of Plassey
events.detail: Robert Clive's victory over Siraj-ud-Daulah marked the beginning of British territorial expansion in India.

events.title: Indian Rebellion
events.detail: The Sepoy Mutiny, led by Mangal Pandey, was the first major organized revolt against British colonial rule.

events.title: Indian National Congress Founded
events.detail: Surendranath Banerjea and others founded the INC, which became the main vehicle for independence struggle.

events.title: Partition of Bengal
events.detail: British partitioned Bengal, sparking Swadeshi movement and mass nationalist awakening across India.

events.title: Salt March (Dandi March)
events.detail: Gandhi led 78,000 people to the sea to make salt, challenging the British salt monopoly — a pivotal moment.

events.title: Quit India Movement
events.detail: Gandhi launched 'Quit India' campaign demanding immediate British withdrawal; mass arrests followed.

events.title: Independence
events.detail: India gained independence on August 15, 1947, ending nearly 200 years of British colonial rule.

title: Rise and Fall of the Mughal Empire
subject: History

events.title: Mughal Dynasty Begins
events.detail: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the Battle of Panipat, establishing the Mughal Empire in India.

events.title: Akbar's Reign Begins
events.detail: Akbar became emperor at age 13 and expanded the empire to its greatest territorial extent.

events.title: Jahangir's Cultural Peak
events.detail: Jahangir continued Mughal artistic and architectural traditions, commissioning magnificent palaces and gardens.

events.title: Taj Mahal Completed
events.detail: Shah Jahan completed the Taj Mahal in Agra — one of the world's greatest monuments to love and architecture.

events.title: Aurangzeb's Expansion
events.detail: Aurangzeb's strict policies and endless military campaigns weakened the empire's finances and stability.

events.title: Empire Begins to Decline
events.detail: After Aurangzeb's death, the Mughal Empire fragmented into regional kingdoms; British power began rising.

events.title: Last Mughal Emperor
events.detail: Bahadur Shah Zafar II, the last Mughal emperor, was exiled to Burma after the 1857 rebellion.

events.title: Cell Discovery
events.detail: Robert Hooke observed 'cells' in cork tissue under his microscope — the first observation of cells.

events.title: Living Cells Observed
events.detail: Anton van Leeuwenhoek saw living organisms (bacteria and protozoa) in pond water using improved microscopes.

events.title: Cell as Unit of Life
events.detail: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck proposed that the cell is the basic unit of living organisms (cell theory developing).

events.title: Nucleus Discovered
events.detail: Robert Brown identified the nucleus in orchid cells — a major structural component of cells.

events.title: Cell Theory Formalized
events.detail: Schleiden & Schwann proposed all plants and animals are made of cells; cells come from pre-existing cells.

events.title: Virchow's Contribution
events.detail: Rudolf Virchow confirmed 'omnis cellula e cellula' (all cells come from cells) — completing cell theory.

events.title: Electron Microscope Invented
events.detail: The electron microscope revealed cell organelles (mitochondria, ER, Golgi) at unprecedented magnification.

events.title: Indus Valley Civilization
events.detail: The Indus Valley Civilization flourished with planned cities (Harappa, Mohenjo-daro) and advanced urban planning.

events.title: Vedic Period Begins
events.detail: Indo-Aryan peoples arrived in India, composing the Vedas — the foundation of Hinduism and Indian philosophy.

events.title: Mauryan Empire Founded
events.detail: Chandragupta Maurya established the Mauryan Empire, the first major centralized Indian empire.

events.title: Ashoka's Reign
events.detail: Emperor Ashoka conquered most of India and promoted Buddhism, leaving rock edicts across the empire.

events.title: Chola Empire Rises
events.detail: The Chola Empire emerged in South India, becoming a maritime and cultural powerhouse for centuries.

events.title: Gupta Empire Golden Age
events.detail: Chandragupta II expanded the Gupta Empire — India's 'Golden Age' of art, science, math, and literature.

events.title: Harsha's Reign
events.detail: King Harsha ruled North India, patronizing Buddhism and maintaining a vast empire through diplomacy.

events.title: Static Electricity Observed
events.detail: William Gilbert discovered that rubbing amber produces an attractive force — coining the term 'electricity.'

events.title: Lightning is Electricity
events.detail: Benjamin Franklin's kite experiment proved lightning is electrical, introducing the lightning rod for protection.

events.title: First Electric Battery
events.detail: Alessandro Volta created the voltaic pile, the first device to produce a steady electric current.

events.title: Electromagnetic Induction
events.detail: Michael Faraday discovered that changing magnetic fields produce electric current — foundation of electric generators.

events.title: Electric Light Bulb
events.detail: Thomas Edison perfected the incandescent light bulb, making electric lighting practical and affordable.

events.title: Alternating Current (AC) Wins
events.detail: Nikola Tesla's AC system defeated Edison's DC, becoming the standard for power distribution worldwide.

events.title: War Begins in Europe
events.detail: Germany invaded Poland on September 1, 1939, triggering Britain and France to declare war on Germany.

events.title: Germany Invades Soviet Union
events.detail: Operation Barbarossa saw Germany launch the largest invasion in history, bringing the USSR into the war.

events.title: Japan Attacks Pearl Harbor
events.detail: Japan's surprise attack on Pearl Harbor brought the United States into WWII as an active combatant.

events.title: Battle of Midway Turning Point
events.detail: The US Navy defeated Japan at Midway, reversing Japanese dominance in the Pacific War.

events.title: D-Day Invasion
events.detail: Over 150,000 Allied troops landed on Normandy beaches, beginning the liberation of Nazi-occupied Europe.

events.title: Germany Surrenders
events.detail: Hitler's suicide and Soviet forces in Berlin forced Germany's unconditional surrender on May 7, 1945.

events.title: Atomic Bombs on Japan
events.detail: US dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki; Japan surrendered on September 2, ending WWII.

events.title: Early Matter Observations
events.detail: Renaissance scientists began classifying matter as solid, liquid, or gas based on observable properties.

events.title: Boyle's Law
events.detail: Robert Boyle discovered that pressure and volume of a gas are inversely proportional (PV = constant).

events.title: Charles's Law
events.detail: Jacques Charles found that gas volume increases proportionally with temperature at constant pressure.

events.title: Avogadro's Law
events.detail: Amedeo Avogadro proposed equal volumes of gases contain equal numbers of molecules — linking moles to volume.

events.title: Critical Point Discovered
events.detail: Thomas Andrews showed gases can become liquids at high pressure/temperature (critical point phenomenon).

events.title: Bose-Einstein Condensate
events.detail: Scientists created a fifth state of matter (Bose-Einstein condensate) by cooling atoms near absolute zero.

events.title: Planck's Quantum Hypothesis
events.detail: Max Planck proposed energy comes in discrete packets (quanta) to solve the blackbody radiation problem.

events.title: Einstein's Photoelectric Effect
events.detail: Einstein explained how photons (light quanta) knock electrons from metals, revolutionizing physics.

events.title: Bohr's Quantum Jumps
events.detail: Niels Bohr proposed electrons jump between fixed energy levels, emitting or absorbing specific light frequencies.

events.title: Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle
events.detail: Werner Heisenberg showed you cannot simultaneously know a particle's position and momentum precisely.

events.title: Schrödinger's Wave Equation
events.detail: Erwin Schrödinger developed the wave equation describing quantum systems as probability waves.

events.title: Copenhagen Interpretation
events.detail: Bohr & Heisenberg proposed particles exist in superposition until measured — the standard quantum interpretation.
